title: Guilford Little League softball tops Vermont to advance to New England Regional championship game - NewsBreak
text:
BRISTOL — The Guilford Little League softball majors (10-12) team was just looking to have a good time when they reached the Eastern Regional tournament two summers ago as part of the town’s minors (8-10) team. Guilford is all business at this summer’s New England Regional tournament and it’s making it look too easy. Guilford scored all of its runs in the first two innings Wednesday night as it needed just 3.5 innings — and a little over an hour — to dispatch of Champlain Little League of St. Albans, Vt., 10-0, at Breen Field to advance to Friday’s championship game. “It was for fun,” Guilford’s Leah Michalowski said about the 2023 trip to regionals. “We didn’t really want to win anything. This tournament we actually want to push and win everything.” Guilford will play the winner of Thursday’s eliminator game between Champlain and Bonny Eagle of Buxton, Maine in Friday’s final at noon at the same site. It will be broadcast live on ESPN. Guilford has won its three Regional games by a combined score of 32-2. And it’s needed just 13.5 innings to do it. “I said it the other day — I did not expect them to dominate,” Guilford head coach Andrea Klein said. “I did have high hopes without a doubt, but to outscore (teams) the way we’ve been (doing) at this level is really something.” Note that Guilford had to fight its way out of the elimination bracket to win the state Final Four. It played five games over six days, concluding with back-to-back wins over Fairfield to win it all. “We’re just coming out really strong and just believing in each other,” Guilford’s Maeve Eagleson said. Eagleson pitched a four-hitter with nine strikeouts and a walk. She also hit an RBI triple in Guilford’s six-run first inning and scored twice. Michalowski hit a bases-clearing double in the bottom of the second and finished with four RBIs and a run. Olivia Mahon also doubled and scored twice. Guilford took a 6-0 lead with one out in the bottom of the first after just seven batters. It did so on four hits, three wild pitches and two errors. “Man, we came out firing on all cylinders right out of the game,” Klein said. “I’ve never seen them start so strong, so fast, as they did tonight. “They were just so motivated to make it to the championship.” Reagan Klein had an RBI single in the first inning in addition to Eagleson’s RBI triple. Guilford continued to pour it on in the bottom of the second inning. Leadoff hitter Abby Volpe was hit by a pitch, Mahon doubled her over to third and Eagleson walked to load the bases. Michalowski followed with a three-run double to extend Guilford’s lead to 9-0 and took third on the throw home. She then scored on Kali Reinhold’s fielder’s choice. “These guys are mentally there, like, they’re locked in,” Andrea Klein said. “I think we probably surprised a lot of people, Guilford getting this far, but I believe in these guys more than anything.” Maeve Eagleson, Guilford — She threw 47 strikes on 70 pitches and her RBI triple in the bottom of the first began her team’s conga line around the bases.
